cards.text: The people left in Judah asked Jeremiah the prophet to find out what the LORD wanted them to do, and they promised to obey, pleasant or unpleasant. The LORD's answer: stay in the land, don't be afraid of the king of Babylon, and do NOT go to Egypt. Now Jeremiah has finished telling them every word the LORD sent him to say.

cards.question: Azariah son of Hoshaiah, the army commander Johanan son of Kareah, and all the arrogant men answer Jeremiah. What do they tell him?

cards.text: Friend, they ASKED for the answer, PROMISED to obey it, and now they're saying it's made up. They claim the LORD never sent Jeremiah to say, 'You must not go to Egypt to reside there.'

cards.question: If the LORD didn't send that message, the men say somebody else is behind it. Who do they say is stirring Jeremiah up against them?

cards.text: Baruch son of Neriah, Jeremiah's own scribe. Now, I once blamed my oven for a batch I forgot about for forty minutes, but blaming the SCRIBE? That's a whole new level.

cards.question: The men claim Baruch wants to hand them over to the ___ so they'll be put to death or exiled to Babylon.
After all that, Johanan and all the army commanders obey the LORD's command to stay in the land of Judah.

cards.text: Johanan and the commanders gather up the whole remnant of Judah, even people who had come back from the nations where they'd been scattered. That means everyone Nebuzaradan, Babylon's captain of the guard, had let stay with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the man Babylon had put over the land.

cards.question: Along with the men, the women and the children, who else is in the group Johanan takes?
Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah get left behind in Judah.
The whole group heads into the land of Egypt. How far do they go?

cards.text: All the way to Tahpanhes, and the text says why: they did not obey the voice of the LORD. That's like typing the address into the GPS YOURSELF and then ignoring every single turn.
Here's the thing about the word of the LORD, friend: it doesn't need a passport. Right there in Tahpanhes, it comes to Jeremiah.

cards.question: The LORD gives Jeremiah something to do while the Jews in Tahpanhes watch. What is it?

answers.text: Bury large stones in the pavement
Break a clay jar by the gate
Wear a yoke through the streets

cards.question: Jeremiah buries the stones in the clay of the brick pavement at the entrance to ___ palace in Tahpanhes.
Then Jeremiah tells the people what those stones mean. The LORD of Hosts says He will send for someone. Who?

cards.text: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. The very king they were afraid of, and the LORD calls him 'My servant.'

cards.question: What does the LORD say He will set over the stones Jeremiah buried at Pharaoh's palace?

cards.text: His THRONE, with his royal pavilion spread over it. That's like dodging your boss all week, finally finding a quiet spot, and your boss walks in and moves his desk right there.

cards.question: According to the LORD, Egypt will be a safe place from the king of Babylon.

cards.text: Nebuchadnezzar will come and strike down the land of Egypt. Death for those destined for death, captivity for those destined for captivity, and the sword for those destined for the sword.

cards.question: The LORD says Nebuchadnezzar will ___ the temples of the gods of Egypt and take their gods as captives.

cards.text: The LORD kindles the fire, and Egypt's gods get carried off as captives. Then Nebuchadnezzar wraps himself with the land of Egypt, like a shepherd wrapping himself in his garment.

cards.question: The LORD says Nebuchadnezzar will leave Egypt unscathed.

cards.text: He will demolish the sacred pillars of the temple of the sun and burn down the temples of the gods of Egypt. We'll leave the remnant in Egypt for now, friend, but trust me, this story isn't done.

findings.problem: The opening card retells Jeremiah 42 (the people asking Jeremiah to inquire of the LORD, promising to obey 'pleasant or unpleasant,' and the LORD's answer to stay in the land, not fear the king of Babylon, and not go to Egypt). It cites only Jeremiah 43:1, so these outside facts have no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Azariah son of Hoshaiah appears here for the first time, and the card never says who he is. Johanan gets a description ('the army commander'), but Azariah does not.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The card states that they asked for the answer and promised to obey it. Those facts come from Jeremiah 42, but the card cites only Jeremiah 43:2.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The card calls Baruch 'Jeremiah's own scribe.' That fact comes from outside the passage (e.g. Jeremiah 36:4), and the card cites only Jeremiah 43:3.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't click. Blaming the oven for his own forgetfulness is set up as the baseline, but nothing shows why blaming the scribe is 'a whole new level.' The escalation has no logic a stranger would get right away.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining. If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: 'That means everyone Nebuzaradan... had let stay with Gedaliah' treats the remnant and the people Nebuzaradan left with Gedaliah as the same group. Verses 5-6 list them as separate items alongside the men, women, children and king's daughters, so the card defines a connection the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The card calls Gedaliah 'the man Babylon had put over the land.' That fact comes from outside the passage (Jeremiah 40:5), and the card cites only Jeremiah 43:5-6.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: 'The very king they were afraid of' relies on Jeremiah 42:11 ('Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon, whom you now fear'). The card cites only Jeremiah 43:10.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: 'with his royal pavilion spread over it' puts the pavilion over the throne. Verse 10 says he will spread his royal pavilion over the stones ('over them').

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: 'The LORD kindles the fire, and Egypt's gods get carried off... Then Nebuchadnezzar wraps himself' tells the prophecy as events happening in the passage. Verse 12 is the LORD's promise of what He will do. The cards around it correctly use 'will.'

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The story-continues line 'but trust me, this story isn't done' nearly copies the doc's example line ('Trust me, friend, this story's not done') instead of being written fresh.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
